headline: High: Kestra can write, execute, and exfiltrate workflow data while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and provides no isolation, creating default-path leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable tool surface and no shared channel is documented, while B can read/write files and process stdin/stdout. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file handoff, so prompt injection is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-generated text into A-facing prompts or course materials
IF A is wrapped in a workflow that feeds B outputs through files or stdin/stdout
mitigations: Use a strict copy-paste policy with human review
Prefix imported text with provenance labels
Disable automatic file handoff between the agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers around B outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and reads/writes local files, while A is a course repo with no documented isolation or data-class restrictions. If they share a workspace, B can ingest and transmit A-related files or logs by default; A itself does not leak, but the pair creates a realistic workspace-to-egress path.
conditions: IF A and B are mounted on the same filesystem or workspace
IF B is given access to files containing sensitive inputs, logs, or artifacts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict B's network egress to approved destinations
Store sensitive inputs outside shared paths
Review B's file access permissions before launch
requires-engineering: add per-file allowlists and DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem; A is non-runnable and has no locking or coordination surface. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory, B can overwrite or race on artifacts and workflow files, and uncertainty about A's actual runtime only increases risk.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory
IF B is allowed to modify git state, workflow definitions, or shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Make shared paths read-only for one agent
Run only one writer at a time
Check in changes through a single merge gate
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on workflow definitions, notifications, and external systems, so if it consumes A-produced content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. A is a course repo rather than a verified planner, but the pair still supports an unverified-to-action path through B's orchestration surfaces.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text, configs, or examples as executable workflow input
IF B sends notifications or runs tasks without a verification step
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Validate A-derived inputs against schemas
Mark A outputs as non-authoritative by default
Log and review all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between generation and execution

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B clearly handles logs, inputs, artifacts, and cloud data. Because the pair lacks explicit compliance metadata, only a limited compliance gap is plausible, and the uncertainty keeps this below medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's workflows
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not configured in Kestra
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Document retention settings for B
Review export and deletion behavior
Restrict cloud-region usage
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
